questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try something different. I have always wanted to go to Iceland

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was unfortunately not very satisfied with the university.

questions.answer: Easy - they hosted 2 meeting and their website is rather good.

questions.answer: I received some emails, and they hosted a meeting on the first day with additional information.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The student housing offered rooms both in the city center and on or near campus. Some had shared kitchens and bathrooms, while others were student apartments with a small kitchen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I thought it was great - a bit expensive. I has the feeling that almost all exchange student were living in student housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy. They had a step-by-step guide on their webpage.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The guide mentioned above.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very successful. I got all the classes I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some of the students I had classes with also took one or two courses outside the law faculty, in subjects that were related to law in some way. I was a bit disappointed that I didn’t try that as well, since they all seemed to really enjoy those courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I was not as satisfied as I had hoped to be. They made many changes during the semester, and almost none of the teachers followed the syllabus. One of the teachers, whom I had in two different courses, became upset and then started ‘punishing’ us with random exams during the semester. She also did not acknowledge that some students may need or are entitled to extra time during exams. We all gathered together to file a complaint, but the university did not acknowledge the issues.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall, the academic level was easier than at KU. However, they expected a lot of work during the semester, which was different from what I was used to. In all courses, I had to submit a 3000-word paper in order to be allowed to take the exam at the end of the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were no big lectures, only seminars. The classes were also a bit smaller than what I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: EU/EEA law I and II, Natural Ressources Law, International Economic Law and Law of the Sea.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend International Economic Law and Law of the Sea. In both courses, the teachers were very nice and passionate. They really tried to make the classes interesting and made the exchange students feel welcome. They also included more recent texts and issues that were relevant. 

However i would not recommend EU/EEA law.

questions.answer: Food and alcohol are very expensive—even compared to Denmark.

questions.answer: Candy and public transport (when you buy a ticket for a month)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a very cheap gym at the university. It was not the best gym, but compared to the price it was quite decent. The university gym also offered yoga classes and volleyball. In addition, the university also organized a running event which was rather fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The facilities mentioned above, as well as a student bar called "the student cellar" under the university. It was open every day, and almost every week student organizations hosted events such as concerts, pub quizzes or speed dating. The book shops also hosted some events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The student cellar was really nice. I would also encourage people to join the gym if they enjoy sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Iceland is a car country... There are basically no local buses outside of Reykjavik. However, renting a car is not as expensive as it might sound. I would definitely recommend exploring Iceland (going on hikes, visiting waterfalls, and going horseback riding). If it is too expensive to do activities every weekend, I would also recommend visiting the swimming pools. They are very nice and also count as a local experience.
However be aware of the harsh weather conditions.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was generally easy to adjust to the local culture, as it is quite similar to Denmark (some people can even speak a bit of Danish). However, the weather conditions and the darkness were definitely a challenge at the beginning.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to talk to people from the beginning in class. Also attend social activities. They are all very good at english.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At the moment, I cannot come up with any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pool. They were so nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. In winter, it gets very dark, so I recommend going outside and exploring whenever the sun is out.
2. I would recommend applying for student housing. I had the impression that those who found accommodation privately felt a bit left out, as many activities took place at the student housing (not just parties).
3. At the beginning, I was very careful with my money, as the country is generally very expensive. However, I would recommend not being overly strict with your budget the whole time. You did not travel all the way to Iceland to live on pasta with pesto and do nothing. Instead, I would recommend allowing yourself (if possible of cources) to explore, spend some money on experiences, and treat yourself once in a while.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to avoid taking the EU/EEA Law course if possible. Be aware that the weather can be quite harsh, and make sure to bring warm clothes. If you are on a budget and do not have all the gear for outdoor activities, there are many good second-hand shops. I bought a very nice hiking jacket there and some gloves. However, you should not be fooled by the weather—when the sun is out, it is one of the most beautiful countries in the world.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met so many nice people and saw the most beautiful nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The people and the nature.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I was generally very happy with my stay; however, if you are looking for academic challenges and structure, I would not recommend Iceland.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
